note: Common fraud patterns in India, written as general awareness. Reporting routes: national cyber crime helpline 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in.

patterns.title: Fake KYC update
patterns.body: A message says your bank KYC, SIM or wallet will be blocked today unless you update it through a link or app. The link leads to a fake page that steals your login, card or OTP. Banks do not block accounts by SMS link; update KYC only in the official app or branch.

patterns.title: OTP or PIN request
patterns.body: Someone posing as a bank, delivery company or government office asks you to read out an OTP or PIN. Anyone with your OTP can complete a payment. No genuine organisation asks for it.

patterns.title: Pay-to-receive UPI trick
patterns.body: A buyer or 'refund desk' sends a collect request or QR code and says to enter your UPI PIN to receive money. Entering a PIN always sends money; receiving money never needs a PIN.

patterns.title: Instant loan app
patterns.body: An app promises a loan in minutes with no documents, deducts large fees, charges very high interest and asks to read your contacts and photos, later used for harassment. Borrow only from banks and lenders regulated by RBI and check the lender's name before you borrow.

patterns.title: Part-time job or task scam
patterns.body: You are offered money for liking videos or rating hotels. Small payments arrive at first; then you must deposit money to unlock bigger tasks and the money is never returned.

patterns.title: Guaranteed-return investment group
patterns.body: A WhatsApp or Telegram group shares 'sure-shot' stock tips or a trading app promising fixed daily or monthly returns. Genuine investments cannot guarantee returns; check that any advisor is registered with SEBI.

patterns.title: Lottery, prize or KBC winner message
patterns.body: You are told you have won a lottery, prize or contest you never entered and must pay a tax or processing fee to claim it. Real prizes do not ask winners to pay first.

patterns.title: Fake customer care number
patterns.body: A number found through search or social media pretends to be customer care and asks you to install a screen-sharing app or share card details. Use only the number printed on your card or the official website.

patterns.title: Electricity disconnection threat
patterns.body: A message says your electricity will be cut tonight because of an unpaid bill and asks you to call a personal number. Check the bill in your electricity board's official app or office.

patterns.title: Courier, customs or 'digital arrest' call
patterns.body: Callers posing as police, customs or courier staff say a parcel in your name has illegal items and that you are under 'digital arrest', then demand money to clear your name. Police do not arrest people over video calls or ask for payments to settle cases.
